podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bowie's Fascination
podcast.body: David Bowie remained fascinated with "The Legendary Stardust Cowboy" and his music until Bowie's own death, despite not meeting Norm O'Dam until 1998. This enduring fascination underscores the profound impact Norm's outsider art had on a major mainstream icon. "By the way, David Bowie never met the man until 1998, and he remained fascinated with him until his death."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for David Bowie's "Stardust"
podcast.body: When David Bowie signed with Mercury Records in 1970, he received a stack of 7-inch singles, which included Norm O'Dam's "Paralyzed." Bowie, who was "no stranger to chemicals in those days," became obsessed with the record and the artist, eventually appropriating the "Stardust" part of "The Legendary Stardust Cowboy" for his iconic Ziggy Stardust character. "Bowie appropriated the Stardust part of the legendary Stardust cowboy for his new creation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspiration for Ziggy Stardust
podcast.body: Norman O'Dan, a Texas proto-psychobilly singer also known as The Legendary Stardust Cowboy, was a big fan of space travel and admired by David Bowie. He was one of the two people who inspired the name for Bowie's alien rock star character, Ziggy, in *The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and The Spiders from Mars*. "And that name was inspired by two people, Bowie's new friend Iggy Pop, and a Texas proto-psychobilly singer named Norman O'Dan, who went by the handle of the legendary Stardust Cowboy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mention in Outsider Music History
podcast.body: The Legendary Stardust Cowboy is listed among artists previously covered as examples of outsider music, alongside Wesley Willis, The Shags, and others. "On those programs, I covered Wesley Willis, the Shags, the legendary Stardust cowboy, Jandic, Captain B. Fart, Daniel Johnson, Florence Foster Jenkins, and even Charles Manson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Legendary Stardust Cowboy Persona
podcast.body: Norman Odom, a "wacky space travel obsessed Texas singer," adopted the stage name The Legendary Stardust Cowboy, from whom David Bowie drew inspiration for the "Stardust" surname in his Ziggy Stardust character. "Norman Odom, a wacky space travel obsessed Texas singer who went by the name the legendary Stardust cowboy."

xref.title: Creation of Ziggy Stardust
xref.body: Building on glam rock concepts, Bowie developed the character Ziggy Stardust. This persona was inspired by the outrageous behavior of Iggy Pop and The Stooges, the artsy "scummy" persona of Lou Reed and the Velvet Underground, the "god-alien" self-perception of Vince Taylor, and the "space travel obsessed" persona of Norman Odom, also known as the Legendary Stardust Cowboy. Bowie combined these influences, changing "Iggy" to "Ziggy" and adopting "Stardust" as the surname. "He invented an entire character completely rooted in glam rock concepts that borrowed from the outrageous behavior of another new friend, Iggy Pop... So Bowie, taking all this information, changed Iggy to Ziggy and adopted Stardust as a surname and thus Ziggy Stardust was born."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Glam Rock Inspirations
xref.body: Bowie's full dive into Glam Rock was inspired by Mark Bolan, his "crazy new friend" Iggy Pop, another friend Lou Reed, and a 1968 seven-inch single called "Paralyzed" by "The Legendary Stardust Cowboy." Drawing on his background as an actor and mime, Bowie meticulously experimented with makeup and costuming. "Inspired by Bowen, his crazy new friend Iggy Pop, Lou Reed, another new friend, and a seven inch single from 1968 called Paralyzed by a guy calling himself the legendary Stardust Cowboy. Bowie went all in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Glam Rock Transformation - Haircut and Fashion
xref.body: Inspired by Marc Bolan, Iggy Pop, Lou Reed, and The Legendary Stardust Cowboy, Bowie went "all in" on glam rock. A key element was his haircut, replicated and modified from a model in a magazine wearing Kansai Yamamoto clothes, razor-cut at the sides and back, backcombed into a "puffy fluff ball," and dyed reddish-orange at Yamamoto's suggestion. This, combined with makeup and costuming, transformed him into the "elfin cute boy in the dress" to something "never before seen in music." "Bowie fun to picture of a model in a magazine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence of Norman Odom (Legendary Stardust Cowboy)
xref.body: Norman Odom, a "wacky space travel obsessed Texas singer" known as the Legendary Stardust Cowboy, provided inspiration for the "Stardust" surname and the cosmic elements of Bowie's Ziggy persona. "He also got inspiration from Norman Odom, a wacky space travel obsessed Texas singer who went by the name the legendary Stardust cowboy."
